story.totalsLine: Across these 10 events the National Weather Service recorded 37 deaths, 1 injury and $18.2 million in recorded damage.

sentences.text: The most significant event in the record for this area was the September 16, 2010 tornado, which the National Weather Service Storm Survey Team confirmed in Queens, impacting Flushing and Bayside with recorded damage of $17,200,000 and 2 deaths.

In Flushing, the survey found the third floor of a residential brick building "severely damaged structurally," and a Pennsylvania woman was killed in her car by a falling tree on Grand Central Parkway.

Heat has been deadly here: in August 2006, the record notes excessive heat resulted in 42 deaths, 14 of them in Queens, and a four-day run of 90-plus temperatures in July 2010 was filed with 4 deaths.

Cold also left its mark, with an arctic air mass in February 2007 bringing subfreezing temperatures for 5 consecutive days, and a January 2000 cold front producing wind chills as low as 30 degrees below 0 at LaGuardia Airport.
On October 29, 2012, a wind gust up to 79 mph was reported near Jackson Heights, and in Flatbush a 30 year old male was killed when a tree fell onto his house.
On January 22, 2016, LaGuardia Airport reported an all time record storm total snowfall of 28.2 inches.
Flooding has proved deadly too: in 2004 flash flooding of roads at College Point involved a fallen power line, and in 2021 a basement apartment on Peck Avenue in Flushing flooded.
Altogether, the National Weather Service recorded 1,232 weather events in this area since 2000, led by High Wind with 174 and Strong Wind with 153.

SE-262537.title: Tornado, Sep 16, 2010
SE-262537.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-262537.text: Tornado on Sep 16, 2010 in QUEENS (county NYC081). Deaths: 2. Injuries: 1. Recorded damage: $17,200,000 (about $17.2 million).
SE-262537.quote: A National Weather Service Storm Survey Team confirmed a tornado in Queens.||The tornado impacted Flushing and Bayside. In Flushing, on Browne Street between Roosevelt and 38th Avenues, the third floor of a residential brick building was severely damaged structurally. Large tree tops were lying on top of buildings and shot like projectiles between buildings. Sides of houses were peeled back. There was clear evidence of twisted metal along the side of the building. On Warren Street near the intersection of Roosevelt Avenue, a steel framed water tower was blown over on the roof. There was a partial roof collapse on another residential building.||A Pennsylvania woman was killed in her car by a falling tree on Grand Central Parkway. Her passenger was injured. A man trying to assist the woman suffered a brain aneurysm and died.

SE-5531650.title: Heat, Aug 1, 2006
SE-5531650.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-5531650.text: Heat on Aug 1, 2006 in Queens (forecast zone NYZ076, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 14. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-5531650.quote: An oppressive air mass moved slowly east across the region from August 1 to August 3. This was preceded by a hot dry air mass, when temperatures reached at least 90 degrees for 5 consecutive days at LaGuardia Airport, from July 27 to July 31.Excessive heat occurred mainly from noon to midnight each day for 3 consecutive days. High temperatures ranged mainly from the upper 90s to around 100 degrees. With surface dew point temperatures in the mid 70s, heat indices ranged from 105 to 115 degrees.Excessive heat resulted in 42 deaths and scattered power outages that lead to business losses.In Southeast NY, excessive heat was responsible for 42 deaths; 40 in New York City; as follows: 14 in Queens, 14 in Brooklyn, 9 in Manhattan, and 3 in the Bronx. This information was provided by the NYC Office of Chief Medical Examiner.

SE-14175.text: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill on Feb 4, 2007 in Queens (forecast zone NYZ076, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 4. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-14175.quote: An arctic air mass caused subfreezing temperatures across the local area for 5 consecutive days; from February 4th through February 8th.|During this time, the daily mean temperature averaged nearly 15 degrees below normal.|Based on a report by the NYC Medical Examiner's Office, hypothermia, was a direct cause of at least 11 fatalities during and after this period of extreme cold in New York City.

SE-5127569.title: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, Jan 17, 2000
SE-5127569.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-5127569.text: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill on Jan 17, 2000 in Queens (forecast zone NYZ076, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 2. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-5127569.quote: An arctic cold front swept across the region during Sunday afternoon, January 16th. Strong and gusty northwest winds combined with well below normal temperatures and produced extremely low wind chill values mainly from midnight to 10 am on January 17th and from 1 am to noon on January 18th.On January 17th, wind speeds from 15 to 20 mph combined with temperatures from 5 to 10 degrees above 0, produced wind chill values from 15 to around 20 degrees below 0 in New York City and from 20 to 30 degrees below 0 across the Lower Hudson Valley.On January 18th, wind speeds averaging 15 mph combined with temperatures from 0 to 5 above zero, produced wind chill values from 20 degrees below 0 at Central Park to 30 degrees below 0 at LaGuardia Airport.

items.action: On July 2, 2021, NWS recorded standing water up to the bumpers of cars in Flushing, about 1.3 km from you. If a road is flooded, do not drive through it. Turn Around, Don't Drown.

guidance.text: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don’t Drown!

guidance.source: National Weather Service, Turn Around Don't Drown
guidance.text: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report that over half of all flood-related drownings occur when a vehicle is driven into hazardous flood water.

items.action: A July 17, 2019 NWS report describes a vehicle stuck in high water at 137th Street and 31st Road in Flushing, with the intersection closed. Never drive around barriers blocking a flooded road, because the road may have collapsed under the water.

guidance.source: National Weather Service, Turn Around Don't Drown
guidance.text: Never drive around the barriers blocking a flooded road. The road may have collapsed under that water.

items.action: Basements flooded on 28th Road in Flushing on August 11, 2018, and 29 NWS flood reports sit within 5 km of your address. Homeowner's insurance does not cover flooding. Ready.gov says to buy flood insurance well before a disaster, since a policy can take up to 30 days to take effect.

why.label: 29 flood reports within 5 km, May 31, 2015 to Jul 31, 2025

guidance.text: Purchase flood insurance or renew a flood insurance policy. Homeowner’s insurance policies do not cover flooding. It typically takes up to 30 days for a policy to go into effect, so the time to buy is well before a disaster. Get flood coverage under the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

items.action: An EF0 tornado touched down near Saint Fidelis Catholic Church in College Point on Aug 2, 2018, 3.2 km from you, knocking down trees and power lines. Sign up for your community's warning system, and in a warning go to an interior room away from windows.

guidance.text: Sign up for your community’s warning system. The Emergency Alert System (EAS) and NOAA Weather Radio also provide emergency alerts. If your community has sirens, become familiar with the warning tone.

guidance.source: National Weather Service, What to do during a tornado
guidance.text: At Your House: If you are in a tornado warning, go to your basement, safe room, or an interior room away from windows. Don't forget pets if time allows.
